items.title: Warren Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, March 17, 2018
items.q: And as a matter of fact he hired a young baritone saxophone player who turned out to be my age and his name was Laurdine “Pat” Patrick.

ctx.x: Can you remember your first paying gig?

Yeah. Working with my father in the Elks Club. Because the Elks Club would have regular Friday night or Saturday night affair and my father broke me in as the drummer when I was fourteen years old. And as a matter of fact he hired a young baritone saxophone player who turned out to be my age and his name was Laurdine “Pat” Patrick. And Pat Patrick of course went on to be one of Sun Ra’s band leaders and he came to New York and we did Broadway shows together and all kinds of things together. And in fact we wound…

I just think it’s so fascinating with yourself, and then you mention Pat Patrick, that you can play Broadway music and something that takes a whole lot of discipline, and then you can be in an environment that is so demanding that you be creative and improvisatory. I just think that’s really interesting.
